actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is a collection of manipulation tasks built with mjlab
The task table lists a Reach task that moves the gripper to a target and a Lift task that lifts a cube (state-based)
The task table also lists a vision-based Lift-RGB task and a Lift-Any-RGB task over 12 objaverse objects
The robot placeholder {Robot} is one of Droid, xArm, Kuka, Gen3 or UR5e
Each robot is a bare-arm MJCF under robots/<name>/xmls/; no gripper is part of it because a gripper is attached at task time
Each robot's constants file returns a RobotCfg with the home pose and the tool-attach offset
The robot MJCF models are sourced from MuJoCo Menagerie
The project depends on mjlab
The package registers the mjlab.tasks entry point named mjlab_manipulation
The MJCF model is named franka_droid
The model compiles its angles in radians
The model uses the implicitfast integrator
The arm default class gives its joints armature 0.1 and damping 1 and gives its position actuators inheritrange 1
joint_1 has the range -2.7437 to 2.7437 rad
joint_2 has the range -1.7837 to 1.7837 rad
joint_3 has the range -2.9007 to 2.9007 rad
joint_4 has the range -3.0421 to -0.1518 rad
joint_5 has the range -2.8065 to 2.8065 rad
joint_6 has the range 0.5445 to 4.5169 rad
joint_7 has the range -3.0159 to 3.0159 rad

The model has seven position actuators named joint_1 to joint_7, with kp 4500 and kv 450 for joint_1 and joint_2, kp 3500 and kv 350 for joint_3 and joint_4, and kp 2000 and kv 200 for joint_5 to joint_7
Droid's ARM_ACTUATORS covers joint_1 to joint_7
Droid's ARM_HOME places the base at (0, 0, 0.5) and sets joint_2, joint_4 and joint_6 to -1/5*pi, -4/5*pi and 3/5*pi radians
Droid's robot config attaches the tool to link_7 at position (0, 0, 0.107) with quaternion (0.7071068, 0, 0, 0.7071068)
The attached gripper actuator targets the split tendon with a position command
The gripper is attached at the robot's tool-attach frame with the gripper/ prefix

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the MJCF text for the joint dimensions, the actuator control ranges and the option time step, but it integrates a placeholder motion of each actuated joint and does not run MuJoCo's dynamics

the stand-in loads no mesh, material or collision shape and resolves no contact, equality, tendon or sensor constraint; the model's meshes and the gripper that the tasks attach at task time are not simulated
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine

only the card's models[0], droid.xml, is served; gen3.xml, kuka.xml, ur5e.xml and xarm/hand.xml (plus xarm/xarm.xml and the Robotiq 2f85 gripper) are other robot models and are not part of this driver
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model's time step only

snapshot and restore use the bridge fallback that copies the time, qpos, qvel and ctrl arrays and the tick count, because the stand-in has no integration-state snapshot; a restore reproduces those arrays but no derived MuJoCo quantity
the model sets no <option timestep>; the stand-in uses MuJoCo's library default, a placeholder, and the bridge reports that value
no physical robot is modelled, there is no viewer or rendering, and nothing was validated against Droid hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
